bandReport.notes:
Band b2 = pages p08-p13, printed page numbers 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 28 (EVEN only — the render carries just the English pages of a bilingual booklet; the footer code is 'SDC-S-TRD - A' on every page). Questions per page: p08 Q60-66 (7), p09 Q67-73 (7), p10 Q74-80 (7), p11 Q81-86 (6), p12 Q87-93 (7), p13 Q94-100 (7). All 41 questions Q60-Q100 are present with no gap.

SEAM BEFORE: p07 (printed 16, band b1) was opened and NOT transcribed. It carries Q52-Q59, every one standalone, and Q59 is COMPLETE on it (stem plus all four options, ending the page). No Directions block is left open on p07, so Q60 starts cleanly and firstComplete is true.

SEAM AFTER: none. p13 is the LAST page of the booklet (14 pages, p00-p13) and the paper GENUINELY ENDS AT Q100 — Q100 prints its stem and all four options in the right column with blank page below and no continuation. lastComplete is true.

DIRECTIONS SETS — exactly ONE in this band, and it opens and closes inside p08, so nothing straddles a seam. D64-66, headed 'For the next three (03) items that follow :', the circus-tent stimulus (right circular cylinder with a right circular cone above it; cylinder height 5 m, cylinder diameter 126 m, total height 21 m). The header line and stimulus are copied verbatim and identically onto all three members and the three are contiguous. The '126 m' and the '5 m' were both re-read at 2.2x — the diameter really is the larger of the two numbers. No other 'Directions' or 'Consider the following for the next N items' block appears anywhere on p08-p13.

STATEMENT-LIST QUESTIONS ARE NOT SETS. Q80, Q83 and Q94 each print a numbered list ('Consider the following : 1. ... 2. ... 3. ...') followed by a 'Which of the above ...' lead-out. Each list belongs to its own single question and is carried in that question's own stem; no context and no setLabel is used for them.

NO FIGURES ANYWHERE IN THIS BAND. Checked at full page and again on crops for every question. hasFigure is therefore not set on any question and no figureNote is emitted. Three things that look like figure candidates and are NOT: (1) Q93 says 'A pie chart depicts ...' but NO pie chart is printed on the page at all — the only datum needed (the 108 degree sector angle) is in the stem, so there is nothing to crop; this is flagged on the question. (2) The geometry and mensuration items Q60-Q63, Q68-Q70, Q84 are all stated entirely in words with no accompanying diagram. (3) There is no data table anywhere in the band, so no GFM pipe table was needed.

NO ANSWER KEY. No key, no marked option and no answer table appears on p08-p13, nor on p07 which was opened for the seam check.

MISPRINTS FLAGGED (transcribed as printed, NOT repaired) — 4 flags, on Q70, Q80, Q84, Q93:
  Q84 option (b) is printed 'Circumference' in a list of triangle centres (Centroid / Circumference / Incentre / Orthocentre). Read at 2.8x; it really is 'Circumference'. This looks like a misprint for 'Circumcentre' but has been left exactly as printed.
  Q70 is printed 'ABCDA is a con-cyclic quadrilateral of a circle ABCD' — a five-letter 'ABCDA' for a quadrilateral, and 'con-cyclic' hyphenated. Read at 2.2x; left as printed.
  Q80 uses a superscript c ('sin 1 degree > sin 1^c') for circular/radian measure; that is the booklet's own notation, recorded as a flag so nobody later reads the c as a typo.
  Q93 as above (pie chart described but not printed).

TWO THINGS THAT LOOK WRONG AND ARE NOT — deliberately NOT flagged, so a later pass does not 'repair' a faithful transcription:
  Q75 pairs the angles crosswise (cosec^2 68 + sec^2 56 - cot^2 34 - tan^2 22). At first glance the pairs look mismatched, but cot 34 = tan 56 and tan 22 = cot 68, so the expression is a well-formed complementary-angle identity as printed. Verified at 3.2x.
  Q61 gives the sides as sqrt(a^2+b^2), sqrt(c^2+a^2) and (b+c) — the asymmetry between the two radicals is what is printed, confirmed at 2.2x.

DECIMALS: this booklet sets decimals with a raised middle dot (81.5, 80.5, 79.0, 78.0 in Q86; 17.4, 16.6, 15.8, 14.2 in Q90; 20.5 in Q88; 1.25 / 0.5 in Q87; 37.5 in Q99; 3.5 / 2.5 / 0.5 in Q87's value list). Every one is transcribed as a FULL STOP per the brief. Each was read at zoom (up to 7x on Q87's third line) to confirm it is a decimal point and not a multiplication sign, and Q87's 'x + 0.5' versus 'x - 0.5' signs were separated at 7x.

EN-DASHES: Q94's class intervals (15–19, 20–24, 25–29 and 15–20, 20–25, 25–30) and Q95's (10–15) are printed with en-dashes and are transcribed with the en-dash as printed. None is inside a table, so none can be confused with a pipe-table separator.

'cosec' is transcribed as an operator (Q75, Q76, Q79, Q83), matching the printed glyph and the convention already used in the sibling band files. A continued fraction (Q100) uses cfrac, not nested frac, per the brief.

OPTION LABELS were read off the page separately for each of (a)-(d) on all 41 questions and never inferred from a neighbour, per the brief's warning about the CDS English mis-slotting defect. This mattered on the SIX questions whose stem sits at the foot of the left column while its options are printed at the TOP of the right column of the same page — Q63 (options at the head of p08's right column), Q70 (c) and (d) at the head of p09's right column, Q77 (c) and (d) at the head of p10's right column, Q90 (options at the head of p12's right column) and Q97 (c) and (d) at the head of p13's right column. In each case this is ordinary two-column flow within ONE page, not a seam.

HIGH-ZOOM CHECKS, all confirming the transcription as written: Q61's four option expressions (2.2x); the D64-66 stimulus figures 5 m / 126 m / 21 m (2.2x); Q70's options 2 sqrt(3) r / 3 and sqrt(3) r / 2, with r OUTSIDE the radical in both (3.0x); Q71's sqrt(7)/2 (2.4x); Q72's exponents 8, 6 and 4 (3.2x); Q73's four option forms (2.6x); Q74's 75 sqrt(3) and 60 sqrt(3) (2.8x); Q75's four angles (3.2x); Q77's options sqrt(3)/4, 1/sqrt(3), sqrt(3), 4/sqrt(3) (3.0-3.4x); Q78's bounds 3/4, 13/16, 1, 2 (2.8x); Q79's numerator and denominator signs (3.2x); Q80's three statements and the superscript c (3.0x); Q83's three statements including 'sin 80 / cos 10' and 'cos 28 cosec 62' (2.8x); Q84's option words (2.8x); Q85's tan 1 ... tan 89 (3.2x); Q87's value list and options (3.0x and 7x); Q90's options (3.2x); Q97's 13^5 + 14^5 + 15^5 + 16^5 divided by 29 (5x); Q98's options 2280 / 2640 / 3820 / 4130 (3.6x); Q100's continued-fraction nesting (3.0x).

SCAN QUALITY: this is the oldest booklet attempted and the scan carries speckle, faint bleed-through and stray marks in the margins. None of it was treated as carrying information; nothing on these pages marks an answer. NOTHING WAS UNREADABLE and no question had to be left out.

SUBTOPICS: every chapter is a catalog key and every subtopic is one of that chapter's listed subtopics — NOTHING WAS INVENTED. Five classification calls worth recording, each a closest fit rather than an exact one. Q63 (rear-wheel revolutions) and Q67 (wheel revolutions at a given speed) are filed under 'Mensuration 2D' / 'Circle, Sector and Segment' because the quantity used is the circumference; Q67 could be argued into 'Time, Speed and Distance'. Q61 and Q68 (area of a triangle from its three sides) are 'Mensuration 2D' / 'Areas of Triangles and Quadrilaterals' rather than 'Triangles'. Q62 (largest triangle in a semicircle) is 'Mensuration 2D' / 'Inscribed and Circumscribed Figures'. Q82 (shadow equal to height) is filed under 'Heights and Distances' / 'Two Object and Shadow Problems' although only one object is involved — that is the only shadow subtopic the catalog offers. Q91 (whether a count is qualitative, discrete or categorical) is 'Statistics' / 'Scales of Measurement', the nearest listed fit for a data-type item.
